notes.summary: FGK2203.12282v2 supplies proved perturbation-friendly subadditivity and mixed-characteristic envelope estimates. Its projective model-resolution and embedded-resolution assumptions remain indispensable.
notes.detailedSummary: The actual source body replaces multiplier ideals with perturbation-friendly ideals, including the vertical correction τ(O,0), asymptotic subadditivity and uniform generation. These prove uniform envelope approximation on a regular model admitting an ample extension. The general envelope theorem retains projective regular domination of every model; the equation theorem additionally retains embedded resolution and skeletal target support. The source does not establish these resolution premises for unrestricted mixed-characteristic varieties.
notes.text:
This is an unverified primary-source scope audit and mathematical deduction, not a complete solution of P16.3.

The exact source is Fang–Gubler–Künnemann, arXiv:2203.12282v2, identifier 28 February 2024, internal date 29 February 2024. Its PDF SHA256 is 0cbd8e3008c97c6635f68ec108b86695b516bf281eef6d788cbb733e69eae029. The saved version was applied, rather than an independently inspected journal text.

Section 4 concerns a flat projective integral regular scheme over a complete mixed-characteristic DVR. Definition 4.1, PDF p6:L14, and Remark 4.2, p6:L30, introduce perturbation-friendly ideals with actual subadditivity. The older +-ideal subadditivity conjecture in Section 3 is not used. Lemma 4.4, p7:L15, and Theorem 4.7, p7:L60–p8, supply the linear-series identity, asymptotic subadditivity and generation. The recursively cited BMP+24 and HLS21 proofs were not independently inspected; their conclusions are imported as expressly stated by FGK.

Here is the checked envelope mechanism. On a regular projective model, let ℒ extend the original ample L, let 𝒜 be an ample extension of the same generic line bundle, and write ℒ=O(D). Set a_m to be the base ideal of ℒ^m, b_m=τ(O,m‖D‖), t₀=τ(O,0), and a′_m=a_m t₀. For large m, a_m is vertical because L^m is generically generated. FGK proves that t₀ is vertical, without assuming it equals O. Coherence gives π^N O⊂t₀⊂O for some N, so log|t₀| is bounded and its correction divided by m tends uniformly to zero.

The published properties are a′_m⊂b_m and b_mℓ⊂b_m^ℓ. Choose a generated ample divisor H and m₀ such that 𝒜^m₀⊗O(−K−(n+1)H) is generated. Apply Theorem 4.7(i) with λ=m and E=mD+H+K. Its required difference E−K−λD equals H and is big and nef. Here n is the special-fiber dimension. Tensoring the two generated sheaves proves generation of b_m𝒜^m₀ℒ^m uniformly in m.

After a principal fiber twist arrange 𝒜=ℒ(−E₀), with E₀ effective vertical. Generation implies a_m+m₀⊃b_m O(−m₀E₀). Write φ_m=m⁻¹log|a_m| and g_E₀ for the bounded model function of E₀. The discrete base-ideal envelope argument, GJKM1712.00980v3 Proposition 2.10, gives φ_m→Pθ(0) pointwise. Passing ℓ→∞ in a′_mℓ⊂b_m^ℓ removes the bounded t₀ correction and gives m⁻¹log|b_m|≥Pθ(0). Consequently, for large k,

φ_k≤Pθ(0)≤[k/(k−m₀)]φ_k+[m₀/(k−m₀)]g_E₀.

Superadditivity of the base ideals gives a common lower bound φ_k≥−C, using finitely many sufficiently large starting indices. Thus

0≤Pθ(0)−φ_k≤m₀(C+‖g_E₀‖∞)/(k−m₀)→0.

Only the sufficiently large tail, where the base ideals are vertical, is required. This verifies the regular-model envelope replacement without reusing characteristic-zero multiplier ideals.

The scope limitations are decisive. Theorem 5.1, p8:L59–p10, requires the regular model and ample extension. Theorem 7.1, p11:L34, extends to every continuous envelope using Definition 6.1, p10:L18: every projective model must admit projective regular domination with unchanged generic fiber. Section 8 additionally assumes Definition 6.3, p10:L34, embedded resolution, to obtain cofinal projective SNC models. Theorem 8.1, p12:L22, retains both premises and SNC-skeleton target support. Remark 6.2, p10:L23, explicitly distinguishes its projective premise from the locally projective arithmetic-threefold result it cites. Therefore that remark does not supply an unconditional mixed-characteristic surface instance of the required hypothesis.

For subsequent notes, source labels denote these exact versions: [F]=FGK2203.12282v2; [M]=Boucksom–Jonsson2307.01697v1; [E]=Boucksom–Eriksson1805.01016v3; [S]=BFJ1201.0187v2; [B]=BFJ1201.0188v1; [G]=GJKM1712.00980v3. The FGK Section 8 reference to Sections 4–6 is printed with BFJ16, while the equation calculus is checked against actual [B] v1. No theorem-number identity is inferred from that printed citation.

Artifacts are P16.3-argument.md, P16.3-paper.tex, source-application-ledger.json and source-extracts/source-provenance.json in /workspace/research/campaigns/round-116/P16.3-original-full-residue-characteristic-reconstruction/artifacts/codex-xAHbiy. Rerun: python3 audit_sources.py. Literal page extracts preserve exact versions and page/line bindings. Hashes establish provenance only.

notes.summary: The whole retained original domain admits test-level orthogonality and strong approximation of finite-dual-energy targets by genuine model Monge–Ampère measures. This does not construct the full E¹ operator or an attained solution.
notes.detailedSummary: For every complete nontrivially discretely valued field, smooth geometrically integral projective variety and actual ample rational polarization, Boucksom–Jonsson2307.01697v1 supplies the characteristic-unrestricted model datum and test orthogonality. Maximizing model tests approximate every positive Radon target of exact mass V=(Lⁿ) and finite model-dual energy, both weakly and in dual energy. All approximating measures are genuine intersection measures. Potential compactness, bounded discontinuous products and realization by an actual E¹ potential remain separate obligations.
notes.text:
This is an unverified model-level mathematical result in the full retained original domain, not a finite-energy surjectivity theorem.

Let K be complete nontrivially discretely valued, X/K smooth geometrically integral projective of dimension n≥1, and L an actual ample rational line bundle. Put V=(Lⁿ)>0. A projective closure of an embedding by a multiple of L gives a nef model reference metric after taking its rational root; no regularity of this closure is assumed. Let θ be its curvature, D the real span of model functions, and Dθ the relatively nef θ-psh model tests on all models of the original X.

For model tests use the genuine mixed intersection measures. On a normal model with special fiber Σb_iE_i, the coefficient at its component divisorial point is b_i times the intersection of the restricted model classes on E_i. The diagonal raw measure MAθ(v) has mass V. Define

𝓔(v)=(n+1)⁻¹Σ_j∫v(θ+ddᶜv)^jθ^(n−j), e(v)=𝓔(v)/V, and m(v)=MAθ(v)/V.

The exact target condition is μ≥0, μ(Xᵃⁿ)=V and 𝓔*θ(μ)=sup_v∈Dθ(𝓔(v)−∫v dμ)<∞. Equivalently ν=μ/V is a probability measure and A=sup_v∈Dθ(e(v)−∫v dν)<∞, with 𝓔*θ(μ)=VA. The entire measure is divided by V; restrictions are never renormalized. Constants cancel because the mass is exact.

[M] Section 1.2.2, PDF p8:L3, provides this synthetic model datum on projective Berkovich spaces over non-Archimedean fields without a residue-characteristic restriction. Model functions are dense in C⁰ and contain constants. The form order is nice: common model determinations express nefness by closed curve-degree inequalities, and ample domination gives spanning. The intersection pairing is positive and symmetric, and its vertical pairing is seminegative by the characteristic-unrestricted local Hodge result expressly imported there. Section 1.3.2, p11:L18, puts the actual ample generic class in its positive Bott–Chern cone; no general identification with the generic numerical space is assumed.

Real nef tests can be uniformly approximated by rational tests after perturbation toward an ample representative on a common higher model and rational approximation within its ample cone. Rational maxima and strict constant margins give the directed-maxima condition. Crucially, [M] Example 2.20, p23:L30, states that its test-level orthogonality always holds in the projective Berkovich setting:

lim_v∈Dθ,v<f ∫(f−v)m(v)=0 for f∈D.

This published conclusion uses relative volumes and the uniformly differentiable estimate cited there. Its recursive BGM22 proof was not independently inspected. It is not an assertion that an arbitrary pointwise envelope is continuous or belongs to the full singular psh cone.

Choose maximizing tests v_j from the finite supremum, and put aν(v)=A−e(v)+∫v dν. Then aν(v_j)→0. For fixed f∈D, [M] Proposition 2.19 supplies a constant C_f independent of v and t such that

|ẽ(v+tf)−e(v)−t∫f m(v)|≤C_f t²,

where ẽ(h)=sup{e(w):w∈Dθ,w≤h}. The dual definition also gives ẽ(v_j+tf)≤A+∫(v_j+tf)dν. Applying the inequalities to f and −f gives

|∫f(m(v_j)−ν)|≤aν(v_j)/t+C_f t for t>0.

First let j→∞ and then t↓0. Density and probability mass prove weak convergence m(v_j)→ν. The absolute values in the published differentiability estimate were visually checked on PDF page 23; they are omitted by the literal text extraction.

For tests define J(u,v)=e(u)−e(v)+∫(v−u)m(u), and J(v)=J(0,v). Uniform concavity at the midpoint, [M] Theorem 1.33, cancels the target's linear terms and gives

J(u,v)≤C_n(aν(u)+aν(v)), and J(v)≤C_n(A+aν(v)).

Thus the maximizing tests have bounded J and are Cauchy for that quasi-distance. The mixed Hölder estimate in [M] Theorem 2.23 gives ∫v_j(m(v_j)−ν)→0. Since e*(m(v_j))=e(v_j)−∫v_jm(v_j), their dual energies converge to A. Multiplication by V gives weak convergence of the genuine raw model measures to μ and the corresponding raw dual-energy convergence.

This result applies to both equal and mixed positive residue characteristic, arbitrary dimension and arbitrary target support. It stops at model-measure approximation. Completeness of the synthetic measure space does not prove that its limit is MAθ(u) for an actual E¹ potential. Defining singular psh metrics by decreasing Fubini–Study nets, as [E] Definition 7.2 permits, likewise does not prove the missing normalized compactness, discontinuous bounded products or unbounded equation theory. [E] Theorem A concerns continuous psh metrics, while Lemma 7.29 and Conjecture 7.30 explicitly separate envelope continuity from that result.

The full proof and source/application ledger are in P16.3-argument.md and source-application-ledger.json. Rerun source checks: python3 audit_sources.py. The original geometric and potential-realization obligations are preserved.

notes.summary: A genuine nef-model example over Q₅ disproves commuting Monge–Ampère with finite-cover averaging. Raw inseparable degree factors and loss of ampleness under nonfinite alterations are additional descent obligations.
notes.detailedSummary: For the degree-two map (z,w)↦(z²,w), blow up the two special points (1,0),(-1,0) on P¹_Z₅×P¹_Z₅. With H=O(2,1) and ε=1/2, the potentials of H−εE₁ and H−εE₂ are nef. The Monge–Ampère vector of their metric average is (31/8,1/16,1/16), whereas the averaged target is (15/4,1/8,1/8). Both have raw mass 4. This rules out arbitrary-solution averaging, not descent of an already invariant solution. Model pullback identities retain finite degree, including radicial maps; a curve-contracting alteration makes the pulled-back polarization nonample.
notes.text:
This is an unverified mathematical diagnostic of a failed descent passage, not a special endpoint substituted for original P16.3.

Take K=Q₅, R=Z₅, Y=X=P¹_K×P¹_K, q(z,w)=(z²,w), and σ(z,w)=(−z,w). The homogeneous square map is finite flat of degree two. For L=O(1,1) on X, its actual pullback is H=O(2,1), of raw volume 4.

Blow up the two distinct special-fiber points (1,0),(-1,0) on the good R-model of Y. This is a projective regular model with multiplicity-one SNC special-fiber components S,E₁,E₂: the strict transform and two exceptional planes. The involution exchanges E₁ and E₂.

For ε=1/2 use A₁=H−εE₁, A₂=H−εE₂, and A_w=H−(ε/2)(E₁+E₂). These classes are relatively nef. On E_i≅P², H restricts trivially, O(E_i) restricts to O(−1), and the other exceptional divisor is disjoint. On S the restrictions are the pulled-back O(2,1) minus the indicated exceptional curves. Let F be the special-fiber curve w=0. For any integral curve C≠F, its multiplicities at the two centers sum to at most F·C≤H·C. Each subtracted coefficient is at most 1/2. For F itself H·F=2 and at most 1 is subtracted. Exceptional curves on S have degree zero or a positive coefficient. This verifies nefness on every special-fiber curve.

Let u,σ*u and w=(u+σ*u)/2 be their genuine model potentials relative to H. On S the exceptional curves are disjoint, have square −1, and have zero intersection with pulled-back H. On E_i the relevant square has degree ε². Therefore

MA_H(u)=(4−ε²)δ_S+ε²δ_E₁,
MA_H(σ*u)=(4−ε²)δ_S+ε²δ_E₂.

The mixed product of A₁,A₂ is 4δ_S: on each exceptional plane one factor is trivial, and on S the two distinct exceptional terms have zero cross intersection. Hence

MA_H(w)=(4−ε²/2)δ_S+(ε²/4)(δ_E₁+δ_E₂),

whereas

[MA_H(u)+MA_H(σ*u)]/2=(4−ε²)δ_S+(ε²/2)(δ_E₁+δ_E₂).

At ε=1/2 these are, in the order S,E₁,E₂, (31/8,1/16,1/16) and (15/4,1/8,1/8). Their difference is (1/8,−1/16,−1/16). Both masses are 4, and all potentials are bounded genuine model potentials. Thus averaging semipositive model metrics does not average their genuine Monge–Ampère measures. The script descent_check.py confirms the exact fractions using Fraction arithmetic; the geometric nefness and intersection argument is the mathematical proof, not that calculation.

This only disproves arbitrary-solution averaging. It does not disprove descent of a solution already invariant under the group, or a route using a correctly pulled-back invariant target and uniqueness. Such a route still needs actual metric-cone and energy descent.

The valid forward model identities for a finite surjective map of degree d with pulled-back metrics are (q*L)ⁿ=dV, q*MA_{q*θ}(q*v₁,…,q*v_n)=d MAθ(v₁,…,v_n), where the first q* on the measure denotes pushforward, and 𝓔_{q*θ}(q*v)=d𝓔θ(v). Consequently normalized energies agree. To avoid the notation ambiguity, the measure identity is equivalently: pushing the upstairs mixed measure down by q gives d times the original mixed measure. These follow term by term from the model intersection projection formula. They are not reverse E¹ descent assertions. Their unbounded extensions require compatible regularization and genuine calculus on both sides.

In equal characteristic p, the relative coordinate Frobenius on Pⁿ_K is finite radicial of degree pⁿ and pulls O(1) back to O(p). It induces an analytic homeomorphism: valuations extend uniquely across purely inseparable residue extensions, and the resulting continuous bijection between proper compact Hausdorff spaces is a homeomorphism. Nevertheless the pulled-back raw model measure has mass pⁿ rather than 1. Topological identification does not erase the degree factor or establish descent of local products.

If a proper generically finite map contracts a curve C, then (q*L)·C=0, so q*L is not ample. An ample equation theorem therefore cannot simply be applied with that polarization on a nonfinite alteration. Adding an ample perturbation changes the class and volume and requires a separately proved limiting and descent theory.

A general cover solution would additionally require finite-dual-energy pullback against all cover tests, invariant psh metric descent, compatible model approximation, genuine mixed products, raw mass, energy cocycles, all original continuous-direction derivatives and comparison. Testing only pulled-back model functions supplies less than finite dual energy against every upstairs test. GJKM's envelope commutation under finite normal ground-field extension does not establish this package for an alteration of varieties. No such package is proved here.

Artifacts: descent_check.py, descent-check-results.json, and Sections 10–11 of P16.3-argument.md. Rerun: python3 descent_check.py. The exact output records the difference [1/8,−1/16,−1/16]; it is one coefficient check, not an exhaustive finite result or a proof of general descent.

notes.summary: A genuine arbitrary-support E¹ equation theorem is derived in mixed characteristic conditional on both exact FGK all-model resolution premises. Original P16.3 remains partial.
notes.detailedSummary: For any complete mixed-characteristic discrete field, smooth geometrically integral projective n-fold and actual ample rational L, assume FGK Definitions 6.1 and 6.3 for every projective model. Cofinal SNC models, compactness and the audited envelopes then support genuine bounded and nonpluripolar mixed E¹ products of raw mass V. Joint integrable weighted limits, every original C⁰-direction derivative, intrinsic finite-dual-energy targets, actual variational attainment and uniqueness modulo constants are checked. The unresolved resolution premises prevent this conditional theorem from solving the original atom.
notes.text:
This is an unverified conditional partial theorem. It does not establish its resolution premises.

THEOREM. Let K be any complete nontrivially discretely valued mixed-characteristic field. Let X/K be a smooth geometrically integral projective n-fold and L an actual ample rational line bundle. Assume BOTH FGK2203.12282v2 Definition 6.1 and Definition 6.3 for the projective models of this particular X. Put V=(Lⁿ)>0 and choose a nef model reference θ. Then the full SNC-based psh cone has genuine approximation-independent bounded and finite-energy mixed products. The diagonal E¹ operator has raw mass V. Every positive Radon μ of mass V satisfying sup_model(𝓔(v)−∫v dμ)<∞ has an E¹ solution, unique modulo additive constants, with arbitrary support. Continuity of the unbounded solution is not asserted. No geometric-origin assumption is added, but the two all-model resolution assumptions are retained.

1. Geometric inputs and full cone. FGK Section 8 gives cofinal projective SNC models under the two premises, and Lemma 6.4 with Remark 6.5 provides ample representatives on sufficiently high models after positive powers. The full cone consists of usc u satisfying u≤u∘p_𝒳 for each SNC determination and whose restriction to each dual complex is a uniform limit of restrictions of θ-psh model functions, exactly [S] Definition 7.1. It is not restricted to functions factoring through one skeleton. FGK expressly transfers [S] Sections 1–7: divisorial determination, weak topology given by uniform convergence on each dual complex, continuity of sup and normalized compactness. Fixed model measures have finite divisorial support, so their integrals are continuous in this topology.

The envelope proof in n1 supplies every continuous envelope and its uniform model approximation. The transferred monotone regularization gives decreasing model approximations, with the sequence construction corresponding to Proposition 4.5 in actual [B] v1. These prerequisites replace the uses of residue characteristic zero; the characteristic-zero multiplier-ideal and vanishing arguments are not reused.

2. Bounded and unbounded operators. The induction in [B] Theorem 3.1 uses model intersections, integration by parts, seminegativity and decreasing regularization. With these prerequisites supplied, it constructs the unique positive bounded mixed operator of raw mass V. Its bounded locality is [B] Theorem 5.1. On continuous psh metrics it agrees with the Chambert–Loir operator.

Set e=𝓔/V on bounded potentials and extend it by the infimum over dominating model psh potentials. The same proof of [B] Proposition 6.2 gives increasing concave weakly upper semicontinuous energy, decreasing-net continuity and e(u+c)=e(u)+c. Define E¹={u psh:e(u)>−∞}.

For u≤0 set u_t=max(u,−t) and define the genuine nonpluripolar measure

MAθ(u)=lim_t→∞ 1_{u>−t} MAθ(u_t), m(u)=MAθ(u)/V.

Bounded locality makes these restricted measures compatible and increasing. The limit is Radon and is unaffected by constant normalization. The bounded pole-set calculus supplies zero pluripolar mass. Full mass is proved: the energy difference formula gives

t m(u_t){u≤−t}≤2(n+1)[e(u_t/2)−e(u_t)]→0.

Here u_t/2 means the truncation at t/2. The difference equals t/2 on the discarded set, and its integral against m(u_t), divided by n+1, is a nonnegative term of the energy difference. Decreasing energy continuity proves the limit. Thus no raw mass is lost.

Comparing two truncations, using their agreement on retained sets and ∫(−u_t)m(u_t)≤(n+1)|e(u)|, gives for continuous f

|∫f m(u_t)−∫f m(u)|≤2(n+1)|e(u)|‖f‖∞/t.

This is uniform for decreasing approximants to u because their energies are bounded below by e(u). Bounded decreasing continuity therefore proves m(u_j)→m(u) for every decreasing E¹ net. The operator is independent of the chosen model approximation.

For mixed inputs u_i≤0, use simultaneous truncations with mixed product T_t and average h_t=n⁻¹Σu_i,t. Positivity of the diagonal expansion gives T_t≤(nⁿ/n!)MA(h_t). On the discarded union B_t=∪{u_i≤−t}, h_t≤−t/n. Concavity bounds e(h_t) below by finite e(h), h=n⁻¹Σu_i, so

T_t(B_t)≤(nⁿ/n!)n(n+1)V|e(h)|/t.

Locality gives compatible restricted products on the complement. Their limit has mass V and equals the independently polarized weak limit, since finite interpolation of the diagonal measures of convex combinations determines every mixed coefficient. This proves positivity, locality and approximation independence of the genuine mixed product.

3. Integrability and joint weighted limits. The proof, rather than the incorrectly signed display, of [B] v1 Lemma 6.10 gives

∫(−w)m(u)≤2^(n+1)(n+1)[−e((u+w)/2)]<∞

for nonpositive u,w∈E¹. Apply it to convex averages and their positive diagonal expansion to get integrability of every E¹ weight against every mixed E¹ measure.

An explicit uniform-tail argument verifies weighted decreasing limits. First take decreasing model inputs with mixed measures T_j and averages h_j, and a decreasing model weight sequence w_l↓w∈E¹. Their suprema have common upper bounds and their energies have finite lower bounds, hence their model J values have a common bound R. For k≥l,

0≤J(w_l,w_k)≤e(w_l)−e(w_k)≤e(w_l)−e(w)→0.

Apply [M] equation (1.37) to w_l,w_k and h_j,0. With m₀=m(0), it gives uniformly in j,k

0≤∫(w_l−w_k)m(h_j)≤∫(w_l−w_k)m₀+C_R[e(w_l)−e(w)]^(2^−n).

For fixed j, its model measure has finite divisorial support, where w is finite, so k→∞ is legitimate by monotone convergence. The right side tends to zero with l, uniformly in j. The mixed domination bound therefore yields sup_j∫(w_l−w)T_j→0. For fixed l the weight is continuous and weak mixed continuity applies. Passing to the limiting measure gives the same tail bound; monotone convergence proves integrability and convergence of the actual w-weighted integrals. A simultaneously decreasing weight is controlled by this same uniform tail. Dominating model approximations and the uniform energy bounds extend the argument to general decreasing E¹ inputs and nets.

Integration by parts and Cauchy–Schwarz consequently pass from models to E¹. The polynomial energies of convex combinations have degree at most n+1; finite interpolation and decreasing energy continuity give coefficient convergence, and the weighted argument identifies those coefficients with actual mixed integrals. Weak convergence is never directly tested against an unjustified unbounded weight.

Bounded locality on retained truncation sets, full mass and zero pole mass give

1_{u>v}m(max(u,v))=1_{u>v}m(u), and ∫_{u<v}m(v)≤∫_{u<v}m(u).

Use max(u,v−ε) and ε↓0 in comparison so equality-locus mass is treated correctly. The mixed polynomial formula gives d/dt|₀₊e((1−t)u+tv)=∫(v−u)m(u).

4. Every original continuous direction. The test orthogonality in n2 becomes actual envelope orthogonality here. For f∈D the increasing directed tests below f converge uniformly to continuous Pθf by Dini's theorem for nets. Uniform continuous-metric operator continuity gives ∫(f−Pθf)m(Pθf)=0. Model-function density, the envelope Lipschitz inequality and uniform operator continuity extend this to every f∈C⁰(Xᵃⁿ). This replaces the separately cited orthogonality proof, without an extra application of an uncached source.

For u∈E¹ and original continuous f, u−|t|‖f‖∞≤Pθ(u+tf)≤u+|t|‖f‖∞, so the perturbed envelope is E¹. Decreasing model u_j give decreasing envelopes converging to Pθ(u+tf): their limit is psh, below u+tf and dominates its envelope. The integrated continuous-envelope derivative identity passes by decreasing energy/operator continuity and dominated convergence:

e(P(u+tf))−e(u)=∫₀ᵗ[∫f m(P(u+sf))]ds.

On the positive side replace f by f+‖f‖∞, obtaining envelopes decreasing to u as s↓0. Subtracting the resulting constant does not change MA. On the negative side use f−‖f‖∞. Decreasing operator continuity proves the genuinely two-sided identity

d/dt|₀ e(Pθ(u+tf))=∫f m(u)

for every original C⁰ direction.

5. Intrinsic targets and actual attainment. Let ν=μ/V and A be its finite model-dual energy. For decreasing model v_j↓u∈E¹,

∫v_j dν≥e(v_j)−A≥e(u)−A.

Together with an upper bound this proves u∈L¹(ν) by monotone convergence, and e(u)−∫u dν≤A. The dual supremum therefore equals its supremum over all E¹. Conversely concavity and mixed integrability give e*(m(u))=e(u)−∫u m(u)<∞, with equality obtained by model approximation. The operator's image has the exact stated finite-energy meaning.

Normalized compactness and continuity of integration against m₀ give a finite T with −T≤∫u m₀≤0 for sup u=0. Set K_C={u psh:sup u=0,e(u)≥−C}. These sets are weakly compact and have 0≤J(u)≤C.

Choose maximizing model tests r_j. Their J values are bounded by n2's defect inequality. [M] Lemma 2.25, with the other test zero, gives |∫v(ν−m(r_j))|≤C_n,R aν(r_j)^(1/2) on bounded-J tests. For u∈K_C take decreasing model u_l. Energy and m₀ integrals converge, so eventually J(u_l)≤C+1. Monotone convergence against ν and the finite-divisorial-support m(r_j) extends the bound with a constant independent of u:

sup_u∈K_C |∫u dν−∫u m(r_j)|≤C_n,R aν(r_j)^(1/2)→0.

The approximating functionals are weakly continuous; their uniform limit proves continuity of target integration on K_C. This is a potential-space argument, not a consequence of completing measures.

Normalize maximizing tests v_j by sup=0. The defect bound gives bounded J, and −e(v_j)=J(v_j)−∫v_jm₀≤J(v_j)+T. They lie in one K_C. A convergent subnet exists; no sequential compactness is assumed. Upper semicontinuity of energy and the proved target-integral continuity give e(u)−∫u dν≥A. The reverse inequality was already proved, so u is an actual E¹ maximizer on X.

For arbitrary continuous f put u_t=P(u+tf) and h(t)=e(u_t)−∫(u+tf)dν. Since u_t≤u+tf, positivity and maximality give h(t)≤A=h(0). The two-sided derivative yields 0=h′(0)=∫f m(u)−∫f dν. Equality against every continuous function gives m(u)=ν and raw MAθ(u)=μ, without a support restriction.

6. Uniqueness. Suppose m(u)=m(v), put f=u−v and S₀=∫f(m(v)−m(u))=0. A model reference change η=θ+ddᶜg preserves the actual operator after replacing u,v by u−g,v−g.
